arxiv-2011-06934.title: Neural network for estimation of optical characteristics of optically active and turbid scattering media
arxiv-2011-06934.creator: Ali Alavi
arxiv-2011-06934.description: Abstract One native source of quality deterioration in medical imaging, and especially in our case optical coherence tomography (OCT), is the turbid biological media in which photon does not take a predictable path and many scattering events would influence the effective path length and change the polarization of polarized light.

arxiv-2203-10215.title: Convergence error analysis of reflected gradient Langevin dynamics for non-convex constrained optimization
arxiv-2203-10215.creator: Kanji Sato, Akiko Takeda, Reiichiro Kawai, Taiji Suzuki
arxiv-2203-10215.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Kanji Sato, Akiko Takeda, Reiichiro Kawai, Taiji Suzuki. Gradient Langevin dynamics and a variety of its variants have attracted increasing attention owing to their convergence towards the global optimal solution, initially in the unconstrained convex framework while recently even in convex constrained non-convex problems. In the present work, we extend those frameworks to non-convex problems on a non-convex feasible region with a global optimization algorithm built upon reflected gradient Langevin dynamics and derive its convergence rates.

arxiv-2303-11433.title: High Resolution Finite Difference Schemes for a Size Structured Coagulation-Fragmentation Model in the Space of Radon Measures
arxiv-2303-11433.creator: Azmy S. Ackleh, Rainey Lyons, Nicolas Saintier
arxiv-2303-11433.description: Abstract In this paper we develop explicit and semi-implicit second-order high-resolution finite difference schemes for a structured coagulation-fragmentation model formulated on the space of Radon measures. We prove the convergence of each of the two schemes to the unique weak solution of the model. We perform numerical simulations to demonstrate that the second order accuracy is achieved by both schemes.

arxiv-2501-16753.title: Overcoming Semantic Dilution in Transformer-Based Next Frame Prediction
arxiv-2501-16753.creator: Hy Nguyen, Srikanth Thudumu, Hung Du, Rajesh Vasa, Kon Mouzakis
arxiv-2501-16753.description: Abstract Next-frame prediction in videos is crucial for applications such as autonomous driving, object tracking, and motion prediction. The primary challenge in next-frame prediction lies in effectively capturing and processing both spatial and temporal information from previous video sequences. The transformer architecture, known for its prowess in handling sequence data, has made remarkable progress in this domain.

arxiv-2601-02225.title: Backscatter-Assisted High-Speed Rail Communications in Straight Tunnel Environments: Effects of Tag Number and Phase Control
arxiv-2601-02225.creator: Yunping Mu, Gongpu Wang, Ruisi He, Theodoros A. Tsiftsis, Saman Atapattu, Chintha Tellambura
arxiv-2601-02225.description: Abstract Backscatter communication is a promising technology to enhance the signal strength received by the receiver in straight tunnel environments. The impact of the number of tags and their phase adjustment on system performance remains a challenging issue though. Therefore, in this paper, we investigate the channel gain of backscatter-assisted communication with multiple tags in straight tunnels.

pmc-11494769.title: Peripheral blood to next-generation sequencing ready DNA library: a novel engineering design for automation
pmc-11494769.creator: Dulguunnaran Naranbat, Lothar à Brassard, Nabil Lawandy, Anubhav Tripathi
pmc-11494769.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Whole genome sequencing (WGS) has become a gold standard for diagnosing genomic variation. Peripheral blood is a common sample source for the extraction of nucleic acids for Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) applications. Here, we present an integrated and fully automated device design that uses new concepts of fluid mechanics, heat-mass transfer, and thermodynamics of enzymatic reactions to extract nucleic acids from the blood and perform DNA library preparation from a pre-filled plate.

pmc-12562175.title: Molecular Docking of Detoxification Enzymes from Oides leucomelaena with Volatiles of Star Anise
pmc-12562175.creator: Yingxue Yang, Zhixiao Zhang, Huifen Ma, Lianrong Hu, Kai Li, Ning Zhao, Ling Liu, Jielong Zhou
pmc-12562175.description: Simple SummaryStar anise is a valuable crop in China, but it is often severely damaged by a pest (Oides leucomelaena Weise). Farmers usually rely on chemical pesticides to control this insect, which can harm the environment. In this study, we aimed to find eco-friendly ways to manage the pest by understanding how it tolerates natural plant defenses.

pmc-12965695.title: Long-term prognostic value of microvascular obstruction by cardiac magnetic resonance in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction
pmc-12965695.creator: Raquel P. Amier, Casper W. H. Beijnink, José F. Rodriguez Palomares, Martijn W. Smulders, Gonzalo Pizarro Sánchez, Rodrigo Fernández-Jiménez, Filipa X. Valente, Albert C. van Rossum, Niels van Royen, Borja Ibañez, Robin Nijveldt
pmc-12965695.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). AimsMicrovascular obstruction (MVO) portends a higher risk of remodelling and adverse events following ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). However, data regarding the implications of MVO in STEMI beyond five years of follow-up are scarce.Methods & ResultsThis is a pooled analysis of three observational studies including 876 prospectively enrolled reperfused first STEMI patients, who underwent cardiac magnetic resonance imaging with late gadolinium enhancement (LGE), between 2003–2019. Median follow-up duration was 6.3 (IQR 3.6–9.3) years. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality.

pmc-12969682.title: Precision diagnosis and therapy for pediatric central nervous system tumors: consensus from the Brazilian Society of Pediatric Oncology (SOBOPE)
pmc-12969682.creator: Kevin Augusto Farias de Alvarenga, Juliana Oliveira de Araújo, Marina Rezende da Silveira, Nicole Souza Silva, Mariah Rocha Coelho, Jéssica Achilles Pimentel, Alcânia Pereira dos Reis, Andrea Maria Cappellano, Bruna Minniti Mançano, Felipe D'Almeida Costa, Flávia Delgado Martins, Gabriela Oigman Bel
pmc-12969682.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryPrecision medicine has reshaped the classification and management of pediatric central nervous system tumors, enabling more accurate diagnoses and targeted therapies. However, access to molecular diagnostics and precision treatments remains uneven in many low- and middle-income countries, including Brazil. To address this gap, the Brazilian Society of Pediatric Oncology (SOBOPE) convened a national expert panel to develop consensus recommendations adapted to the Brazilian healthcare context.

pmc-12994314.title: Development and Validation of the Emergency Department Transitions Measure
pmc-12994314.creator: Sara Beachy, Danielle M McCarthy, Julianna Lenoir, Alexzandra Gentsch, Richard Hass, Marissa Witmer, Paula Ostroff, Melissa Tupas, Lindsey Shughart, Hailey Shughart, Kristin L Rising
pmc-12994314.description: BackgroundTransitions of care are high‐risk periods for patient safety in the emergency department (ED), particularly for patients who are still in the diagnostic process and are discharged with diagnostic uncertainty. Care transitions must be improved for these patients, as one third of discharged ED patients have diagnostic uncertainty.

pmc-13220164.title: Application of 200 kHz Tumor Treating Fields (TTFields) in Patients With Infratentorial High-Grade Glioma: Case Series
pmc-13220164.creator: Carlos Kamiya-Matsuoka, Chirag B Patel, James D Battiste
pmc-13220164.description: Tumor treating fields (TTFields) therapy at 200 kHz is FDA-approved for supratentorial glioblastoma. However, reports of TTFields in patients with infratentorial high-grade glioma (HGG) are rare. Two patients with infratentorial HGG received off-label 200 kHz TTFields. To reduce impaired neck range of motion, the electrode transducer arrays were “skeletonized” by cutting a portion of the adhesive material.

pmc-13313617.creator: I-Hsin Ma, Wei-Lun Huang, Yao-Lin Liu, Yi-Ching Tung, Tzu-Hsun Tsai
pmc-13313617.description: IntroductionDespite contemporary management, the incidence of diabetic retinopathy in adolescents during the first 2–5 years of type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) remains unchanged, underscoring the need to better understand early retinal changes. In this study, we investigated early retinal changes in children with T1DM using optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA).

pmc-13347924.title: Colchicine enhances macrophage cholesterol efflux by targeting DTL-mediated ubiquitination and degradation of ABCA1
pmc-13347924.creator: Lingfei Tong, Wenming Wu, Yan Wang, Lihua Duan, Hui Li
pmc-13347924.description: ObjectiveThis study aims to elucidate the potential pharmacological mechanisms by which colchicine confers clinical benefits in patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, focusing on its effects on cholesterol efflux.MethodsThis study was conducted in multiple cellular models. First, cell viability was assessed and the optimal dosage of colchicine was screened via the Cell Counting Kit-8 assay.

pmc-13361793.title: Design of a Pediatric Low Motor Function Item Battery in leukodystrophies
pmc-13361793.creator: Francesco Gavazzi, Sarah Woidill, Anjana Sevagamoorthy, Abbas F. Jawad, Russell D'Aiello, Jamie Bradford, Miriam Lerner, Peter Hong, Aaliyah White, Zarrin Tashnim, Stacy V. Cusack, Allan M. Glanzman, Ann Harrington, Amy T. Waldman, Adeline Vanderver, Laura A. Adang
pmc-13361793.description: Leukodystrophies are rare genetic disorders that disrupt myelin formation in the central nervous system, leading to a broad range of neuromotor impairment. Standard assessment tools, including the Gross Motor Function Measure-88 (GMFM-88), were designed to favor higher-level skills, like sitting and walking, with more limited sensitivity for earlier developmental skills.

pmc-13369300.title: Muscle oxygenation measured by near‐infrared spectroscopy during resistance training: A scoping review
pmc-13369300.creator: Moath Mohammad, Ghydaa Alshanty, Juliette Langelier, Morgane Mary‐Pouliot, Michael Stolberg, Rami Hammad, Alain Steve Comtois
pmc-13369300.description: Near‐infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) is a noninvasive optical technique used to estimate local muscle oxygenation by measuring hemoglobin‐related variables and muscle oxygen saturation. This information helps understand how skeletal muscles respond to diverse types and intensities of resistance training, giving a clearer picture of metabolic activity during exercise.
